label: GO step right after a broken-fixation penalty at D1
explanation: Fires only at GO, and only when the reward input there is -1, i.e. the agent failed to fixate at this trial D1 and gets a penalty (equivalent to d1_err == 1). It fires on 91% of such steps and almost never elsewhere: dev P=0.97, R=0.98, mass recall 1.00. It never fires at D1 or D2 or on ordinary GO steps. Magnitude: strongest when the premature D1 action was a2 (in_action == 2); adding that condition raises precision to 0.99 but drops the weaker activations, which come from a1 breaks, so I kept the simpler predicate. These D1 errors cluster late in episodes (trials 80-99), at low value and strongly a2-favoring choice logits, so the feature also correlates with value, choice and good == S2, but only as side effects of the error event. Uses only observed inputs.

issues: The core claims check out. All activation is at GO (D1 and D2 have 0 active steps). 91.5% of in_rew==-1 steps are active and they carry 100% of the activation mass. On test the predicate scores P=0.983, R=0.978, F1=0.981, mass recall 0.9996.
All 10 test misses (0.0% of the mass) are tiny activations (about 0.01 of max) on ordinary GO steps. This is noise, not a class the predicate fails to cover.

All 8 test false positives are at window step 1, the first GO step of a window. That looks like a short-history or window-start artifact rather than a missing behavioral condition. It is small and does not change the label.

Minor overclaim: adding in_action==2 is said to raise precision to 0.99. On test it gives P=0.983, the same as the base predicate, while recall drops to 0.90 (F1 0.939). Keeping the simpler predicate is still the right call.
I did not verify the side claims that the errors cluster late in episodes (trials 80-99) and come with low value. They are not part of the predicate.
